## Description

AWEX training can retain MCore/Transformer Engine activation storage after backward, reducing GPU memory available for phase transitions. Add scoped activation tracking and release after the complete backward, while preserving model parameter and buffer storage.

Tracking is enabled only when the engine has AWEX weight residency. Ordinary training does not install the patches or scan/mutate activation storage.

Split from #1613 in response to the independent memory-lifecycle review request: https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/pull/1613#discussion_r4244759121. This feature is not required by the staged AdamW algorithm.

Real CUDA tests cover checkpoint recomputation and storage release with FP32/BF16 across two optimizer steps. Large-model AWEX integration and multi-node behavior remain to be validated on this standalone branch.

## Related Issue

Split from #1613 (activation storage ownership review).

## Type of Change

- [x] ⚡ Performance improvement

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (`pre-commit run --all-files`)
- [x] Relevant tests pass; new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Branch is up to date with `main`
- [x] This PR was created by a coding agent via `/create-pr`

## Additional Context

### Validation

- `pytest -q tests/test_megatron_activation_storage.py`: 5 passed.
- Current activation-storage, Megatron, named-loss, transport and R3 regressions with `-m "not slow or ci"`: **287 passed**, including the five activation-storage cases and real FP32/BF16 CUDA recomputation across two optimizer steps.
- Real CUDA TE/MCore checkpoint recomputation in FP32/BF16: exact two-step gradient, parameter and momentum parity with tracking on/off; nested activation release and model storage preservation.
- Coverage also includes ordinary-training bypass and tracked model aliases.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.

The CI workflow matches main; runner provisioning changes are excluded from this PR.

nodes.body: Thanks for splitting this out and limiting it to the AWEX path. Could we add a real CUDA MCore/TE test with checkpoint recomputation enabled? The current tests do not exercise the patched backward and storage-release lifecycle. Comparing gradients and parameter updates with tracking on/off across at least two training steps would help validate safety before merging.

Added the requested real CUDA recomputation coverage in `f39798ce`, in `tests/test_megatron_activation_storage.py`.

The FP32 and BF16 cases each run two checkpointed TE blocks (LayerNorm, BasicLinear, GELU, BasicLinear, residual) using MCore's actual `make_viewless_tensor` and `CheckpointFunction.backward`. Tracking is enabled for one copy and disabled for an identically initialized reference. Across two SGD-with-momentum steps, the tests require exact equality of every parameter gradient, updated parameter, and momentum buffer; they also verify that nested recomputation actually releases activation storage and preserves parameter/buffer storage pointers and contents. These paths use real CUDA/TE kernels, without mocking MCore/TE internals. Both cases are marked `slow` + `ci` so they run in the GPU CI suite.

Local validation passed:

- Standalone activation-storage suite: 5 passed.
- Activation-storage, Megatron engine, LM head, gradient sync, optimizer config, and transport regressions: 84 passed; one existing slow DCP test deselected by the normal `(not slow or ci)` filter.
- Full `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.

For the previous SGLang CI failure, the check-run annotation reports **"The self-hosted runner lost communication with the server"** while the unit-test step was running; the test log blob is unavailable, so there is no reported assertion failure to fix from that run. The vLLM unit-test job passed. I am retriggering both variants from this PR's `safe-to-test` label on the new commit. Large-model AWEX and multi-node validation remain separate from this focused CUDA regression.

Synced main and addressed the CI startup failure in separate commits:

- `8e64114d`: merge main through 6cad8710; adapt activation call-order and named-loss test harness setup to the current engine. Tracking behavior is unchanged.
- `4b01ec8f`: obtain a fresh runner registration token before every zone-allocation attempt; isolate runner labels and VM creation/cleanup by run ID and attempt.

The previous run failed **before pytest**: SGLang provisioning waited through GCP capacity retries from about 06:37 to 07:37 UTC, then the runner never registered and timed out at 08:28. Both unit-test jobs were skipped. [GitHub documents a one-hour registration-token lifetime](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/self-hosted-runners#create-a-registration-token-for-a-repository); expiry is consistent with the timeline, but VM startup logs are unavailable, so this is not a directly observed registration rejection.

Local validation: **287 related tests passed**, including all five activation-storage cases and actual FP32/BF16 CUDA TE/MCore checkpoint recomputation over two optimizer steps with exact gradient, updated-parameter and momentum parity. Full pre-commit passed. actionlint passed with ShellCheck disabled. Mock-API execution of the actual workflow creation script verified fresh tokens after capacity retry, API failure aborting before allocation, mode-0600 token files and cleanup. No fresh large-model AWEX or multi-node integration run was performed.

Pushed head `4b01ec8f`; the PR is mergeable. Triggered a fresh full CI through this PR's **safe-to-test** label: **[38723318799](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/actions/runs/38723318799)** (in progress, no result yet).

Restored `.github/workflows/test-areal.yml` exactly to main in **67c6bb88**. The file no longer appears in this PR diff; runner/token changes are excluded. Updated the description accordingly. +# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Release activation storage retained by Megatron and Transformer Engine."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import sys
+import weakref
+from collections import deque
+from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+
+import torch
+
+_tracking_installed = False
+_active_tracker: ActivationStorageTracker | None = None
+
+
+class ActivationStorageTracker:
+    """Own activation tensors retained within one training forward/backward."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        protected_tensors: Iterable[torch.Tensor] = (),
+        *,
+        strong_references: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        self._tensor_refs: deque[torch.Tensor | weakref.ReferenceType[torch.Tensor]] = (
+            deque()
+        )
+        self._strong_references = strong_references
+        self._protected_storages = {
+            tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+            for tensor in protected_tensors
+            if isinstance(tensor, torch.Tensor)
+            and tensor.is_cuda
+            and tensor.untyped_storage().nbytes() > 0
+        }
+        self._nested_released_storages = 0
+        self._nested_released_bytes = 0
+
+    def child(
+        self, protected_tensors: Iterable[torch.Tensor] = ()
+    ) -> ActivationStorageTracker:
+        """Create a nested tracker that inherits protected storage ownership."""
+        child = ActivationStorageTracker(protected_tensors, strong_references=True)
+        child._protected_storages.update(self._protected_storages)
+        return child
+
+    def record_nested_release(self, storage_count: int, released_bytes: int) -> None:
+        self._nested_released_storages += storage_count
+        self._nested_released_bytes += released_bytes
+
+    def protect(self, tensors: Iterable[torch.Tensor]) -> None:
+        """Exclude storages whose ownership leaves this tracker scope."""
+        self._protected_storages.update(
+            tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+            for tensor in tensors
+            if isinstance(tensor, torch.Tensor)
+            and tensor.is_cuda
+            and tensor.untyped_storage().nbytes() > 0
+        )
+
+    def append(self, tensor: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        if not tensor.is_cuda:
+            return
+        if tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr() in self._protected_storages:
+            return
+        if self._strong_references:
+            self._tensor_refs.append(tensor)
+        else:
+            self._tensor_refs.append(weakref.ref(tensor))
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def release(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
+        """Release storage after the complete backward has returned."""
+        released_storages: set[int] = set()
+        released_bytes = 0
+
+        while self._tensor_refs:
+            tensor_ref = self._tensor_refs.popleft()
+            tensor = (
+                tensor_ref()
+                if isinstance(tensor_ref, weakref.ReferenceType)
+                else tensor_ref
+            )
+            if tensor is None:
+                continue
+            storage = tensor.untyped_storage()
+            data_ptr = storage.data_ptr()
+            nbytes = storage.nbytes()
+            if data_ptr in self._protected_storages:
+                continue
+            if nbytes > 0 and data_ptr not in released_storages:
+                released_storages.add(data_ptr)
+                released_bytes += nbytes
+                storage.resize_(0)
+            if tensor._base is None:
+                tensor.detach_()
+
+        return (
+            len(released_storages) + self._nested_released_storages,
+            released_bytes + self._nested_released_bytes,
+        )
+
+    def discard(self) -> None:
+        """Drop Python references without mutating an incomplete autograd graph."""
+        self._tensor_refs.clear()
+
+
+def install_activation_storage_tracking() -> None:
+    """Patch Megatron and TE activation boundaries for scoped storage tracking.
+
+    Megatron modules commonly import ``make_viewless_tensor`` into module-local
+    aliases. Replace both the canonical function and aliases already loaded so
+    the tracker records the final tensor returned by ``Function.apply``.
+
+    Transformer Engine's operation fuser marks activation inputs and outputs as
+    non-clearable during backward. Some versions leave the corresponding C++
+    autograd references alive beyond the backward call. Selective recompute also
+    builds a nested autograd graph inside ``CheckpointFunction.backward``. Track
+    normal forward boundaries weakly so tracking does not extend their lifetime.
+    During checkpoint recompute, hold boundaries strongly only for the lifetime
+    of the nested backward and release them as soon as its checkpoint returns.
+    """
+    global _tracking_installed
+
+    if _tracking_installed:
+        return
+
+    from megatron.core import utils as megatron_utils
+
+    original_make_viewless_tensor = megatron_utils.make_viewless_tensor
+
+    def tracked_make_viewless_tensor(
+        inp: torch.Tensor, requires_grad: bool, keep_graph: bool
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        output = original_make_viewless_tensor(inp, requires_grad, keep_graph)
+        tracker = _active_tracker
+        if tracker is not None and keep_graph and inp._base is not None:
+            # Megatron's viewless tensor aliases ``inp`` storage. Track that
+            # shared activation storage and release it only after its owning
+            # backward scope completes; cloning here would retain one full
+            # hidden-state allocation per layer and inflate the forward peak.
+            tracker.append(output)
+        return output
+
+    for module_name, module in tuple(sys.modules.items()):
+        if not module_name.startswith("megatron.") or module is None:
+            continue
+        if (
+            getattr(module, "make_viewless_tensor", None)
+            is original_make_viewless_tensor
+        ):
+            module.make_viewless_tensor = tracked_make_viewless_tensor
+
+    from transformer_engine.pytorch.ops import fuser as te_fuser
+
+    original_fuser_call = te_fuser.OperationFuser.__call__
+
+    def tracked_fuser_call(
+        fuser: te_fuser.OperationFuser,
+        input_: torch.Tensor,
+        *extra_inputs: torch.Tensor,
+        **kwargs: object,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+        output = original_fuser_call(fuser, input_, *extra_inputs, **kwargs)
+        tracker = _active_tracker
+        if tracker is not None:
+            tracker.append(input_)
+            if isinstance(output, torch.Tensor):
+                tracker.append(output)
+            else:
+                for tensor in output:
+                    tracker.append(tensor)
+        return output
+
+    te_fuser.OperationFuser.__call__ = tracked_fuser_call
+
+    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel import random as tensor_parallel_random
+
+    original_checkpoint_backward = tensor_parallel_random.CheckpointFunction.backward
+
+    def tracked_checkpoint_backward(ctx: object, *grad_outputs: torch.Tensor):
+        global _active_tracker
+
+        tracker = _active_tracker
+        if tracker is None:
+            return original_checkpoint_backward(ctx, *grad_outputs)
+
+        # A checkpoint recompute builds a complete nested graph during its own
+        # backward. Keep its activation ownership local so each checkpoint can
+        # release immediately instead of retaining every layer until the full
+        # model backward returns. Checkpoint inputs and output gradients belong
+        # to the outer graph and must never have their shared storage resized.
+        checkpoint_inputs = getattr(ctx, "saved_tensors", ())
+        nested_tracker = tracker.child((*checkpoint_inputs, *grad_outputs))
+
+        def pack_hook(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+            if not tensor.is_leaf:
+                nested_tracker.append(tensor)
+            return tensor
+
+        def unpack_hook(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+            return tensor
+
+        _active_tracker = nested_tracker
+        try:
+            with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks(pack_hook, unpack_hook):
+                result = original_checkpoint_backward(ctx, *grad_outputs)
+        except BaseException:
+            nested_tracker.discard()
+            raise
+        finally:
+            _active_tracker = tracker
+
+        nested_tracker.protect(
+            tensor for tensor in result if isinstance(tensor, torch.Tensor)
+        )
+        released_storages, released_bytes = nested_tracker.release()
+        tracker.record_nested_release(released_storages, released_bytes)
+        return result
+
+    tensor_parallel_random.CheckpointFunction.backward = staticmethod(
+        tracked_checkpoint_backward
+    )
+    _tracking_installed = True
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def track_activation_storage(
+    protected_tensors: Iterable[torch.Tensor] = (),
+) -> Iterator[ActivationStorageTracker]:
+    """Scope activation storage tracking to one training forward/backward."""
+    global _active_tracker
+
+    if _active_tracker is not None:
+        raise RuntimeError("Megatron activation storage tracking is already active")
+    tracker = ActivationStorageTracker(protected_tensors)
+    _active_tracker = tracker
+    try:
+        yield tracker
+    except BaseException:
+        tracker.discard()
+        raise
+    finally:
+        _active_tracker = None

@@ -0,0 +1,181 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+from contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from areal.engine import megatron_engine as engine_module
+from areal.engine.megatron_utils.activation_storage import (
+    ActivationStorageTracker,
+    install_activation_storage_tracking,
+    track_activation_storage,
+)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("awex_residency", [False, True])
+def test_training_tracks_activation_storage_only_for_awex(monkeypatch, awex_residency):
+    """Ordinary training bypasses tracking; AWEX releases after one backward."""
+    engine = engine_module.MegatronEngine.__new__(engine_module.MegatronEngine)
+    engine._weight_residency = (
+        SimpleNamespace(ensure_grad_buffers=lambda: None) if awex_residency else None
+    )
+    engine.model = [torch.nn.Linear(2, 2)]
+    engine.model[0].config = SimpleNamespace(calculate_per_token_loss=True)
+    engine.hf_config = None
+    engine._ensure_ready = lambda: None
+    engine._normalize_batch_input = lambda batch: (batch, None)
+    engine.optimizer_zero_grad = lambda: None
+    engine._prepare_mb_list = lambda *args, **kwargs: SimpleNamespace(mbs=[{}])
+    engine._per_token_loss_multiplier = lambda *args: 1.0
+    engine._collect_mtp_loss = lambda count: None
+    calls = []
+    engine.forward_backward_batch = lambda *args, **kwargs: calls.append("backward")
+
+    def optimizer_step():
+        calls.append("optimizer")
+        return {}
+
+    engine.optimizer_step = optimizer_step
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        engine_module, "record_training_batch", lambda *args: nullcontext()
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        engine_module, "tensor_container_to", lambda value, device: value
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        engine_module,
+        "install_activation_storage_tracking",
+        lambda: calls.append("install"),
+    )
+
+    def release():
+        calls.append("release")
+        return 0, 0
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def tracking(protected):
+        assert {id(t) for t in protected} == {
+            id(t) for t in engine.model[0].parameters()
+        }
+        yield SimpleNamespace(release=release)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(engine_module, "track_activation_storage", tracking)
+    engine.train_batch({}, lambda *args: None, lambda *args: None)
+    assert calls == (
+        ["install", "backward", "release", "optimizer"]
+        if awex_residency
+        else ["backward", "optimizer"]
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA is required")
+def test_tracker_releases_activation_and_preserves_model_alias():
+    """A tracked view of model storage must stay resident after release."""
+    model_param = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.ones(8, device="cuda"))
+    activation = torch.ones(8, device="cuda")
+    tracker = ActivationStorageTracker([model_param])
+    tracker.append(model_param.view(2, 4))
+    tracker.append(activation)
+
+    released, size = tracker.release()
+
+    assert released == 1
+    assert size == 8 * activation.element_size()
+    assert activation.untyped_storage().nbytes() == 0
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        model_param, torch.ones_like(model_param), rtol=0, atol=0
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.slow
+@pytest.mark.ci
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA is required")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_cuda_te_checkpoint_tracking_preserves_two_training_steps(
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> None:
+    """Real TE recomputation preserves gradients, updates and persistent storage."""
+    from megatron.core import utils as mcore_utils
+    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import checkpoint
+    from transformer_engine.pytorch import ops
+
+    class RecomputeModel(torch.nn.Module):
+        def __init__(self) -> None:
+            super().__init__()
+            self.blocks = torch.nn.ModuleList(
+                [
+                    ops.Sequential(
+                        ops.LayerNorm(16, device="cuda", dtype=dtype),
+                        ops.BasicLinear(16, 32, device="cuda", dtype=dtype),
+                        ops.GELU(),
+                        ops.BasicLinear(32, 16, device="cuda", dtype=dtype),
+                    )
+                    for _ in range(2)
+                ]
+            )
+            self.register_buffer("offset", torch.ones(16, device="cuda", dtype=dtype))
+            self.forward_modes = []
+
+        def forward(self, inputs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+            hidden = inputs + self.offset
+            for block in self.blocks:
+
+                def recompute(value, block=block):
+                    self.forward_modes.append(torch.is_grad_enabled())
+                    viewless = mcore_utils.make_viewless_tensor(
+                        value.view_as(value), requires_grad=True, keep_graph=True
+                    )
+                    return block(viewless) + value
+
+                hidden = checkpoint(recompute, False, hidden)
+            return hidden
+
+    torch.manual_seed(123)
+    baseline = RecomputeModel()
+    tracked = RecomputeModel()
+    tracked.load_state_dict(baseline.state_dict())
+    models = [baseline, tracked]
+    optimizers = [
+        torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.05, momentum=0.9) for model in models
+    ]
+    install_activation_storage_tracking()
+
+    for step in range(2):
+        inputs = torch.randn(8, 16, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+        target = torch.randn_like(inputs)
+        gradients = []
+        for model, optimizer, enabled in zip(models, optimizers, [False, True]):
+            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+            protected = [*model.parameters(), *model.buffers()]
+            pointers = [tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr() for tensor in protected]
+            context = track_activation_storage(protected) if enabled else nullcontext()
+            with context as tracker:
+                output = model(inputs.detach().clone().requires_grad_())
+                loss = (output.float() - target.float()).square().mean()
+                loss.backward()
+            if tracker is not None:
+                assert tracker._nested_released_storages > 0
+                count, size = tracker.release()
+                assert count > 0 and size > 0
+            gradients.append(
+                [parameter.grad.clone() for parameter in model.parameters()]
+            )
+            assert model.forward_modes[step * 4 :] == [False, False, True, True]
+            for tensor, pointer in zip(protected, pointers):
+                assert tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == pointer
+                assert tensor.untyped_storage().nbytes() > 0
+            optimizer.step()
+
+        for reference, actual in zip(gradients[0], gradients[1]):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, reference, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        for reference, actual in zip(baseline.parameters(), tracked.parameters()):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, reference, rtol=0, atol=0)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                optimizers[1].state[actual]["momentum_buffer"],
+                optimizers[0].state[reference]["momentum_buffer"],
+                rtol=0,

issue_comments.body: Thanks for splitting this out and limiting it to the AWEX path. Could we add a real CUDA MCore/TE test with checkpoint recomputation enabled? The current tests do not exercise the patched backward and storage-release lifecycle. Comparing gradients and parameter updates with tracking on/off across at least two training steps would help validate safety before merging.

Added the requested real CUDA recomputation coverage in `f39798ce`, in `tests/test_megatron_activation_storage.py`.

The FP32 and BF16 cases each run two checkpointed TE blocks (LayerNorm, BasicLinear, GELU, BasicLinear, residual) using MCore's actual `make_viewless_tensor` and `CheckpointFunction.backward`. Tracking is enabled for one copy and disabled for an identically initialized reference. Across two SGD-with-momentum steps, the tests require exact equality of every parameter gradient, updated parameter, and momentum buffer; they also verify that nested recomputation actually releases activation storage and preserves parameter/buffer storage pointers and contents. These paths use real CUDA/TE kernels, without mocking MCore/TE internals. Both cases are marked `slow` + `ci` so they run in the GPU CI suite.

Local validation passed:

- Standalone activation-storage suite: 5 passed.
- Activation-storage, Megatron engine, LM head, gradient sync, optimizer config, and transport regressions: 84 passed; one existing slow DCP test deselected by the normal `(not slow or ci)` filter.
- Full `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.

For the previous SGLang CI failure, the check-run annotation reports **"The self-hosted runner lost communication with the server"** while the unit-test step was running; the test log blob is unavailable, so there is no reported assertion failure to fix from that run. The vLLM unit-test job passed. I am retriggering both variants from this PR's `safe-to-test` label on the new commit. Large-model AWEX and multi-node validation remain separate from this focused CUDA regression.

Synced main and addressed the CI startup failure in separate commits:

- `8e64114d`: merge main through 6cad8710; adapt activation call-order and named-loss test harness setup to the current engine. Tracking behavior is unchanged.
- `4b01ec8f`: obtain a fresh runner registration token before every zone-allocation attempt; isolate runner labels and VM creation/cleanup by run ID and attempt.

The previous run failed **before pytest**: SGLang provisioning waited through GCP capacity retries from about 06:37 to 07:37 UTC, then the runner never registered and timed out at 08:28. Both unit-test jobs were skipped. [GitHub documents a one-hour registration-token lifetime](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/self-hosted-runners#create-a-registration-token-for-a-repository); expiry is consistent with the timeline, but VM startup logs are unavailable, so this is not a directly observed registration rejection.

Local validation: **287 related tests passed**, including all five activation-storage cases and actual FP32/BF16 CUDA TE/MCore checkpoint recomputation over two optimizer steps with exact gradient, updated-parameter and momentum parity.
